pr_title: Fix `min_id` and `max_id` causing error in search API
pr_comments:
There are two issues with this PR:
- it does not allow timestamps, which the previous version allowed and the specs account for
- the specs still refer to `FilterValidationError`

> could we add some example date values which previously triggered errors but with this change now do not trigger errors to those specs to avoid future regression?

Looks like this portion didn't happen. If someone confirms the nature of the error values here, I can do this as followup.

@mjankowski The errors that were fixed were from passing an ISO-8601 datetime into the `before:`/`after:` syntax, specifically from the output of `Mastodon::Snowflake.to_time(123456...)` which happens when `min_id` or `max_id` are passed to the API.

issue_context.title: Search with `max_id` or `min_id` always fails with `422 Invalid date`
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. make API call to search for statuses with a max_id, e.g. `https://mastodon.online/api/v2/search?q=search&type=statuses&max_id=113404702919566475`

Alternatively, using Ivory:
1. Perform any search (e.g. for the word “search”)
2. Scroll down far enough that it tries to load the next page of results, or refresh so it tries to load newer results

### Expected behaviour

Returns statuses with IDs below given max_id or above min_id

### Actual behaviour

422 Invalid date, with a date that was not in the request (example above returns `{"error":"Invalid date 2024-10-31T23:47:20Z”}`)

### Detailed description

This affects all searches in Ivory (probably other clients as well) which appears to use the min_id and/or max_id parameters for pagination

### Mastodon instance

mastodon.online, mastodon.gamedev.place

### Mastodon version

v4.3.1

### Technical details

The full error log entry from Ivory (with request and response headers) looks like:

comments: Data point: testing with Pachli shows that searches using the `offset` parameter instead of `m.._id` are not affected.
This is almost surely due to #31526 rejecting datetimes that are not only dates.

To add some more context: `offset` is the recommended way to paginate through search results, but `min_id`/`max_id` are also supported, and internally converted to ISO-8601 datetimes, which are rejected by the regexp introduced in https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/31526.

That regexp needs to be edited to support optional time in such datetimes.

Is there a particular reason `offset` is recommended? Since the results for a given `offset` value aren’t stable over time as more posts get made, it’s not really feasible to use in a user-focused app where we don’t know how long the user will wait before trying to load the next page.
